reforms.description: The tax treatment of human capital investment has been improved through enhanced deductions for tuition and increased contribution limits to Registered Education Savings Plans, which support post-secondary education savings.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improving tax treatment for education investments encourages more individuals to pursue higher education, thereby enhancing the skilled workforce.
reforms.status_evidence: The reform has been put into effect as stated.
reforms.importance_rationale: While it is a significant reform, it does not represent a structural change to the system.
reforms.source_quote: The tax treatment of human capital investment has been improved. Deductions for tuition and for students attending educational institutions have been enhanced, and contribution limits to Registered Education Savings Plans... have been increased.

reforms.description: The federal government announced a ten-year research and development fund with an allocation of C$ 500 million to support innovation and technological advancement.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The allocation of funds for R&D is expected to stimulate innovation and technological advancements, contributing positively to economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The fund has been established and is operational.
reforms.importance_rationale: This funding initiative is significant but does not represent a major overhaul of the funding system.
reforms.source_quote: Ontario tabled its budget which included... C$ 500 million for a ten-year research and development fund.

reforms.description: The Canada Foundation for Innovation was established with a funding commitment of C$ 800 million over five years to enhance research infrastructure and support innovation, aiming to modernize research infrastructure at post-secondary institutions and hospitals.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investing in research infrastructure is crucial for fostering innovation and improving the capacity for scientific research.
reforms.status_evidence: The foundation has been established and is operational.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a major structural change in the funding and support of research infrastructure.
reforms.source_quote: The creation of a Canada Foundation for Innovation to modernise and enhance research infrastructure at post-secondary institutions and hospitals.

reforms.description: The Canadian government introduced a refundable R&D tax credit for small firms, broadening the definition of R&D and technology for tax purposes, alongside additional funding for the Industrial Research Assistance Program (IRAP) to stabilize its funding and incentivize R&D activities in high unemployment regions.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: These measures are designed to stimulate private sector investment in R&D, which is essential for innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The reforms have been enacted and are currently in effect.
reforms.importance_rationale: While significant, these reforms do not represent a major overhaul of the innovation support system.
reforms.source_quote: The recent Budget announced additional funding for the Industrial Research Assistance Program (IRAP) to stabilise its funding at C$ 97 million per year.

reforms.description: The Canadian government created Networks of Centers of Excellence in 1988 to promote collaboration between universities, industry, and government in key areas of research and innovation, with a renewal of the programme in 1997 to support university-industry research partnerships.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Fostering collaboration between sectors enhances knowledge transfer and innovation, which is beneficial for economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The renewal has been completed and the programme is operational.
reforms.importance_rationale: The renewal of the programme is significant but does not represent a major structural change.
reforms.source_quote: The recent Budget announced the renewal of the Networks of Centres of Excellence (NCE) programme with stable funding of C$ 47 million per year.
